items.title: QUIC and Covert: Novel HTTP/3-Powered RATs Target Southeast Asian Governments
items.summary:
Unit 42 uncovered a cyberespionage campaign targeting Southeast Asian governments.
The attackers used PerfectPioneer RAT, modular KUKURAT, and stealth HTTP/3 C2 channels.

items.title: Google Project Zero Slashes Bug Disclosure Deadlines, Splitting Experts
items.summary:
Google Project Zero announced it will shorten public disclosure timelines for vendors from 120 days to 30 days.
The change will roll out over the next 14 months.

items.title: Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach
items.summary:
Infoblox is investigating a SharePoint breach that exposed customer and staff data.
Details of the breach remain limited.

items.title: California sues OpenAI for Hugging Face and other incidents, alleging deception and recklessness
items.summary:
California filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging deception and recklessness.
The state claims OpenAI withheld incident details from the Attorney General.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Match fined $10 million for alleged Tinder privacy violations
items.summary:
Ireland’s data protection regulator fined Match Group $10 million for Tinder’s failure to provide users with their personal data upon request.
The fine addresses privacy violations.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ‘123456’ has been the world’s most popular password for 7 out of the last 8 years
items.summary:
The password "123456" remains the most commonly used worldwide, dominating for 7 of the past 8 years.
Security experts warn against using simple passwords.

items.title: NoisyTCP bug gives Linux servers a remote crash problem 11 years in the making
items.summary:
A long‑standing NoisyTCP flaw can cause remote crashes on Linux servers.
The vulnerability affects services even when running inside a container.

items.title: Rapid7 Detected Exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center, N-able N-central also Exploited
items.summary:
Rapid7 identified exploitation of CVE-2026-90436, a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability in Apache Axis.
The flaw affected Atlassian Confluence and N‑able N‑central.

items.title: Italian regulator fines Meta $886 million for violating data privacy law
items.summary:
Italy’s data regulator fined Meta $886 million for alleged misuse of Android users’ photo galleries to recommend content.
The fine cites violations of privacy laws.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: King Charles opens new HQ for National Cyber Force, UK’s offensive hacking unit
items.summary: UK's National Cyber Force opens a new headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire, housing the country's offensive cyber operations team.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Crook turns free trials into phishing factory, as LearnWorlds sends 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices
items.summary: LearnWorlds sent 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices to free‑trial users, created 570 bogus accounts and a fake YouTube page, but the CEO denies a breach.

items.title: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
items.summary: Microsoft attributes last week's global Microsoft 365 outage to a software bug introduced in July, which caused cascading failures that left over 80% of gateway servers unresponsive.

items.title: From view-only access to container root: five vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs (FIXED)
items.summary: Rapid7 identified five vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs that allow an attacker with view‑only access to chain exploits and execute arbitrary OS commands as root within the DocumentServer container, also exposing hidden server files and document data.

items.title: Typosquatters Target New Brand Domains Within 24 Hours of Registration
items.summary: Symantec reports attackers target newly registered domains that mimic well‑known brands within 24 hours, using lookalike sites to facilitate malicious follow‑on activity.

items.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
items.summary: Fandango Media confirms a data breach that exposed payment card details entered on its checkout pages and advises customers to monitor accounts.

items.title: Google Project Zero Sets Course for 30-Day Disclosure Deadline
items.summary: Google Project Zero will adopt a 30‑day vulnerability disclosure window starting January 2028, moving from a 60‑day window in February 2027 to accelerate responsible disclosure.

items.title: La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Breach Exposes 22 Million People
items.summary: Maileva, a La Poste subsidiary, suffered a breach that exposed names and postal addresses of 22 million individuals.

items.title: 7 Tips For Complying with CJIS Password and MFA Requirements
items.summary: The FBI’s CJIS Security Policy now requires stronger passwords and MFA for all accounts. Specops Software outlines seven steps to meet these requirements, block compromised passwords, and maintain compliance.

items.title: British government ‘complacent’ on cyber threats from hostile states, peers warn
items.summary: A National Resilience Committee report warns that the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill falls short of necessary security standards. The report was released before a key vote on the legislation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: EU sanctions pro-Russia hackers, two dozen staff at Kremlin disinformation contractor
items.summary: The EU sanctioned a pro‑Russian hacktivist group and about 24 employees of the Moscow firm behind the Doppelgänger disinformation campaign.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Lithuanian customs agency restores services after cyberattack, possible data breach
items.summary: Lithuanian Customs shut down its main user‑management portal after a November 10 attack. Services were restored over the weekend, but a potential data breach remains possible.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in 60 days
items.summary: Microsoft announced that Windows Server 2016 will reach end of support in 60 days and will no longer receive security updates. Customers are urged to migrate to supported versions.

items.title: Telegram Widgets Hit by RCE Demos, Malware Warning Days After Launch
items.summary: Kaspersky reports that Telegram’s new widgets may be exploitable to deliver WebRAT. Researchers demonstrated remote code execution, while Telegram founder disputes the claims.

items.title: Six Unpatched Danfoss Refrigeration Controller Flaws Could Allow Remote Takeover Without Login
items.summary: Six vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK‑SM800A refrigeration controllers allow remote takeover without authentication. No patch is available, and firmware 5.4.0 does not fix the flaws.

items.title: Retadup Worm Resurfaces 7 Years After Takedown to Spread CoffeeLoader Malware
items.summary: A new variant of the CoffeeLoader malware was discovered. The installer drops a patched '7z.dll' into a temporary folder and runs it via rundll32.exe to deliver additional payloads.

items.title: Google Project Zero to Cut Disclosure Deadline to 30 Days by 2028
items.summary: Google Project Zero will publish bug details within 30 days of reporting, regardless of whether the issue is fixed, by 2028.

items.title: Usable Security at Luxury Hotels
items.summary: Attackers used fake booking emails to access a hotel reservations inbox, copy legitimate refund requests, and approve fraudulent ones. The incident shows that simple 'don’t click links' advice is insufficient in hospitality settings.

items.title: Microsoft previews remote lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
items.summary: Microsoft previewing Remote Lock for Windows 10/11 and Windows Server 2016‑2022 via Intune. The feature locks a device without wiping, signs out sessions, hides sign‑in options, and displays a lock screen.

items.title: Australian retail giant Coles investigates cybersecurity incident
items.summary: Coles Group is investigating a cybersecurity incident that did not affect its stores. The investigation is ongoing.

items.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑114713 is a high‑severity flaw in UnrealIRCd that lets attackers execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges. It has been exploited in recent attacks.

items.title: Hackers Probe Newly Disclosed Flaws in Copeland Refrigeration Controllers
items.summary: Vulncheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers; two were quickly targeted by threat actors.

items.title: Uber Data Breach Impacts 150,000 People
items.summary: A third‑party services provider was compromised, exposing names, addresses, and driver’s license numbers of 150,000 Uber drivers.

items.title: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 blocks fewer security tasks, while Mythos gets better at finding bugs
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 with coding and reasoning improvements. Security task handling and bug detection performance were noted.

items.title: Unpatched GeoVision camera software gave cryptojackers a side door into 13 organizations
items.summary: Unpatched GeoVision camera management software was used by attackers to access Windows machines in 13 organizations, turning them into cryptocurrency miners between Nov 8‑10.

items.title: Information Commissioner’s Office Receives 300+ Reports of Medical Snooping
items.summary: The UK Information Commissioner’s Office received over 300 reports of unauthorized insider access to medical files in 2024.

items.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
items.summary: Linux cryptomining malware SANSAR uses a modified NVIDIA library to mask GPU activity, operates via TOR, and is part of threat cluster REF3364.

items.title: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
items.summary: NoisyTCP, an 11‑year‑old Linux kernel flaw, affects most distributions and can crash Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations.

items.title: Rspamd 4.3.0 stops forwarded mail from softening DMARC rejects
items.summary: Rspamd 4.3.0 fixes bugs that let unauthenticated attackers crash workers or bypass authentication. The update also prevents forwarded mail from softening DMARC rejects.

items.title: Tor Updates DoS Defenses Again as Relay Attacks Continue
items.summary: Tor 0.4.9.17 patches multiple security issues, including a flaw in IPv6 DoS protection, to counter ongoing relay attacks.

items.title: Microsoft pushes Windows emergency updates to fix activation failures
items.summary: Microsoft released emergency out‑of‑band updates to correct Windows activation and licensing failures caused by recent security patches.

items.title: Microsoft Rules Out Cyberattack in Outage, Warns of Phishing Campaign
items.summary: Microsoft stated the outage was not caused by a cyberattack and warned of phishing emails that impersonated Microsoft 365 notices referencing the incident.

items.title: A USB worm’s second life: Retadup spreading CoffeeLoader
items.summary: The old USB worm Retadup, previously seized, is now being used to distribute a new version of the CoffeeLoader malware.

items.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
items.summary: Kaspersky found that the BO Team exploited Log4Shell to compromise a Russian developer’s VMware vCenter and code‑signing server over several months.

items.title: Google Project Zero will disclose bugs after 90 days, fixed or not
items.summary: Google’s Project Zero will publish discovered vulnerabilities 90 days after reporting them, regardless of vendor fixes, with shorter deadlines in 2027 and 2028.

items.title: Ory Hydra: Open-source OAuth 2.0 server and OpenID Connect provider
items.summary: Ory Hydra is an open‑source OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect server that issues and validates tokens without storing usernames or passwords, relying on external identity systems.

items.title: Product showcase: ESET Mobile Security brings phishing protection and security checks to iOS
items.summary: ESET Mobile Security for iOS provides link verification, device security scans, and Wi‑Fi assessment on iOS 18.0+, free to use without an account.

items.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
items.summary: TSMC confirmed a breach of employee data. A threat actor uploaded 6.9 GB of personal information to an online auction. The leak involved sensitive employee records.

items.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’
items.summary: The Pentagon renamed its Chief Data and Analytics Office to the Super Intelligence Office following a directive to replace 'artificial intelligence' with 'super intelligence' in executive branch communications.

items.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
items.summary: Meta was fined €805 million in Italy for a Facebook Android feature that accessed users' photos and videos without explicit consent, with the feature enabled by default.

items.title: Week in review: Secret stealer hits GitHub repos, Claude Code turned into remote-controlled implant
items.summary: A weekly security review highlighted a secret stealer targeting GitHub repositories, the transformation of Claude Code into a remote‑controlled implant, and guidance on handling leaked credentials.

items.title: Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Android Gallery Photos and Videos on Facebook
items.summary: Meta faced a $887 million fine in Italy for accessing Android gallery photos and videos on Facebook without obtaining free and informed consent from users.
